summary: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She was a researcher at the University of Oslo (1993) and a PhD researcher at the University of Bonn (1995), and held posts at the University of Warsaw.

Agathe Keller is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She has held posts at REHSEIS (attested 2006), the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2017), and Paris Diderot University (attested 2017).

Agehananda Bharati was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Vienna. He taught at Delhi, Banaras Hindu, Nava Nalanda, Tokyo, and Kyoto, before serving as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw, and completed her PhD at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~2002–2007), later holding posts at Cornell University (~2008–2010) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

Agvan Dorzhiev was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Monastery and Drepung Gomang Dratsang (1873, 1880–1888), earning a Geshe Lharampa degree. He founded Datsan Gunzechoinei and Atsagat Datsan (1913).

Ahmad Hasan Dani was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied under A. S. Altekar, Mortimer Wheeler, and K. de B. Codrington, holding posts at the University of Dhaka (1950–1962), University of Peshawar (1962–1971), and Quaid-i-Azam University (1971, 1997).
Aiko Okoshi specialized in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1975) and was appointed as a full-time lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bedford College (~1974–1977) and trained under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He was co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery around 2010.

Ajahn Brahm specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Emmanuel College, Cambridge (~1969–1972), he studied under Boonman Poonyathiro and Ajahn Chah, and became abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery around 1995.
Ajahn Khemadhammo works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Drama Centre London (~1963–1966) and trained under the traditional teacher Ajahn Chah (~1972–1977).
Ajahn Pasanno is a Buddhist studies scholar who trained under traditional teacher Ajahn Chah (~1974–1982). He served as the founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2018).

Ajahn Sucitto works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a degree at the University of Warwick (~1968–1971), trained under Ajahn Sumedho starting in 1977, and served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He earned master's degrees from Washington and UC Berkeley (~1961–1963) and trained under Ajahn Chah (1967–1977), later serving as abbot at Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).
Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya studied Indology and Buddhist studies under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya. He held a post at the University of Calcutta as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow.
Akhil Rajeev P specializes in computational fields and Indology. He has held posts at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji Sōgakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao, later holding posts at Ryukoku University, Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle under Yuichi Kajiyama, later holding posts at Kyushu University (1987) and Kyoto University across several roles between 1983 and 2023.

Akihiro Oda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was educated at Otani University. He also held posts there as a full-time lecturer (attested 1992) and as Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Akiko Kikuchi works in Buddhist studies. She was a research student at Minobusan University (attested 2026) and served as a professor at Musashino University (attested 2026).
Akiko Murakawa is an Indologist whose studies were conducted under Harry Falk, Gerhard Ehlers, Masato Fujii, Werner Knobl, Yasuke Ikari, Kazuhiko Yoshida, and Muneo Tokunaga.
